ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, this is a schematic diagram of the metabolic process of a certain substance in a certain microorganism. Besides C, when which other two substances are excessive, might they indirectly inhibit enzyme ①?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows the metabolic pathway in which A is converted into B under the action of enzyme ①, and B is converted into C under the action of enzyme ②. After C, it splits into two branches: one is converted into D under the action of enzyme ③, and the other is converted into E under the action of enzyme ④. The figure also uses “inhibition” to mark that C inhibits enzyme ①, D inhibits enzyme ③, and E inhibits enzyme ④. Then reason: The question asks, besides C, which two substances, when excessive, might indirectly inhibit enzyme ①. Excess D will inhibit enzyme ③, causing the process by which C is converted into D to be blocked, leading to accumulation of C; excess E will inhibit enzyme ④, causing the process by which C is converted into E to be blocked, also leading to accumulation of C. Since C can inhibit enzyme ①, excess D and E can indirectly inhibit enzyme ① by promoting the accumulation of C.
